holes_in_opposing_case: Direct instrument hole vs trend-follower short SOFR_2027-03: they merge two different objects into one 'aligned continuation.' FACT: Sep-16 hike 25bp to 3.75-4.00% was >90% priced; NY Fed SOFR jumped from 3.62 on 2026-09-16 to 3.85 on 2026-09-17; that overnight jump IS the known event settling into the benchmark. FACT: SR3H7 still implies 4.58, +73bp over the new fixing, with Dec-26 already at 4.32. INFERENCE: paying Mar-27 at 4.58 is a second bet that ~three extra 25bp steps remain required after the priced hike printed. Continuation of a delivered, pre-priced 25bp is not evidence that leftover 1H27 premium is too small. UNKNOWN: CME SR3/UST positioning is unavailable, so they cannot claim the trend is under-owned or that a squeeze must extend.

trend-follower mispricing is internally contradictory. They say the strip peaking near SR3U7 4.755 then easing 'requires a cooling that gauges have not shown.' That sentence admits ~90.5bp of extra tightening is already in the path (4.755 vs SOFR 3.85). Shorting SOFR_2027-03 at 4.58 therefore argues that a 1m US 2Y +57bp (z 3.29) to a 1y 100th-percentile 4.76 still underprices the cycle. That is extrapolation of a post-event overshoot, not riding an unpriced hiking trend. The 2Y +9bp 1d after a known hike is the overshoot screen, not independent confirmation of more hikes.

Their invalidation is a one-way bar: only a US inflation/labor BREAK counts; housing-pain or 'the hike was priced' 'alone' do not. Event-premium decay after a fully priced FOMC does not need a growth break. FACT: August CPI already kept a tightening bias and US gauges 72/75/69/74 were known into the decision. Known information cannot explain a NEW 1m 3.3-sigma 2Y squeeze unless an energy/global-hawk overlay is still being added on top of the 25bp. Requiring a data break before fading leftover SR3H7 premium lets that overlay run until it is already in overnight SOFR again.

trend-follower ignores the packet's same-week catalyst that weakens the overlay: Saudi STS crude via Oman reduced the extreme oil-supply tail, while a separate rollup still warns shock absorbers are weakening. Tail-reduced plus residual energy risk is not a mandate to pay duration. They also skip supplied 2s10s analogs for the -18bp 1m flattening (US 2s10s +56bp, 0.6th percentile 1y): 2024-02-26 and 2022-12-14 steepened in the next month; 2022-04-08 steepened 1m then re-flattened; 2023-05-30 kept flattening. Mixed forward outcomes plus inverted 2022-23 starting levels are not a license to add to a 1y front-end extreme. Regime difference: today's 2s10s is positively sloped after a pre-priced hike, not an early-cycle inversion.

rate-hawk long implied-rate SOFR_2027-09 is the same crowded overlay one contract later. They admit the 25bp was >90% priced and US 2Y already +57bp 1m, then want the 2027 terminal ABOVE packet SR3U7 4.755. That is not 'underpriced restraint'; it is asking the 1y 2Y extreme to go further. Their invalidation (SR3U7 retracing the entire 17-Sep SOFR jump AND Dec-26 4.32 pricing less than one 25bp vs overnight 3.85) would already have destroyed a Mar-27 receiver first. The additive mispricing is Mar-27 4.58 versus already-priced Dec-26 4.32 (~26bp of extra 1H27 steps), not a claim that Sep-27 cannot print a higher peak if data re-accelerate.

dollar-king long USDCAD does not identify a stretched USD or a cheap CAD that forces paying US 2027. FACT: ECB mid 1.401047 as of 2026-09-18 is only 74th percentile 1y / 87th 5y, still -1.25% 3m, +1.74% 1m. CA-US 2Y at -140bp (3.8th/4.3rd percentile 1y/5y) matches overnight CORRA 2.29 versus SOFR 3.85 (~156bp): that is a policy ANCHOR, not incomplete FX translation. They themselves cite USDCAD versus CA-US 2Y r^2 0.022. CFTC CAD leveraged funds are still net short -39022 contracts but that net is the 99th percentile 1y after +16426 weekly cover, so long USDCAD fights residual covering. 140bp 2Y USD-over-CAD carry is exactly why we rejected short USDCAD as the expression; carry support for long USDCAD is not a reason to pay leftover SR3H7 hikes.

value-guy receive-SOFR / pay-CORRA 2027 H1 contaminates a valid Mar-27 SOFR receive with a Canada-cheapness fade this seat already rejected. The 156bp overnight gap is the economic anchor, not an overshoot. Paying CRA 3.13/3.365 into Canada labor 38, August employment -42k, wages +2.0% y/y, and CPI-trim/median 1.9%/2.0% is the energy-pass-through crowd, not peer-policy 'fair value.' Analogs are mixed by their own citation: 2025-01-30 at -145bp compressed 25bp over 3m; 2024-12-18 at -130bp cheapened another 20bp over 3m. Do not pay Canada to express a US event-premium fade. Their CAD_UP/USD_DOWN tags can be the FX echo of fading US front-end premium; the CRA pay leg is the hole.

perma-bull pay CORRA_2027-03 (implied 3.13 vs cash 2.29) is the Canada version of the same energy-hawk overlay. Activity 66 and WTI/Brent at the top of the 1y distribution do not override core-near-2% and labor 38. carry-is-king, rate-dove, and positioning-cynic receive 2027 CORRA — a different instrument. The hole is the USD_UP/CAD_DOWN leap: 'BoC will not deliver 84-130bp' does not require USD higher, CAD lower, or short SOFR_2027-03. USDCAD is not a 1y extreme and CAD shorts are already covering. Receiving leftover US hike premium can coexist with a Canada path-premium harvest; it does not require joining their FX tags or switching our book into CRA. We stay off CORRA because the overnight US-CA gap is the anchor, not the discrepancy.

catalyst-junkie long AONIA_2026-10, perma-bear long AONIA 2027 H1, and cross-merchant short AUDCAD (5y percentile 99.96 / z 2.76) are a different stretch: AU housing transmission versus already-restrictive AONIA 4.35. We set aud_view not_relevant because that is not the SOFR leftover-hike discrepancy. USD_UP hitchhiking on the delivered Fed hike does not own Mar-27 leftover US premium. Cross-merchant CAD_UP via BoC catch-up/energy pass-through is the same overlay we fade in US rates, and short AUDCAD fights 164.9bp 2Y / 206bp overnight carry. None of those expressions falsify long SOFR_2027-03.
attack: Strongest opposing claim is trend-follower: price, policy and US gauges are aligned, so fading on 'priced in' is premature. Alignment of still-hot gauges with a hike that was already >90% priced is exactly what a fully priced meeting looks like. The new objects are (i) SOFR already at 3.85 and (ii) SR3H7 still +73bp, after (iii) the extreme oil-supply tail was reduced. Paying 4.58 is not riding that alignment; it is adding the energy-hawk overlay that the last-24h desk thesis already describes as keeping term-rate pressure elevated.

trend-follower and rate-hawk both need a data break or a higher-than-4.755 terminal before they will admit the front end overshot. That is trend-following a 1y 100th-percentile 2Y and a 0.6th-percentile 1y 2s10s flattening after the event is in the overnight fixing. Mean reversion here is not 'the Fed is done' and not a collapse to 3.85; it is partial giveback of additive 1H27 steps toward already-priced Dec-26 4.32. Their expression (pay Mar-27 or pay Sep-27 implied) owns the opposite of that residual.

USD_UP/CAD_DOWN seats (dollar-king, trend-follower, rate-hawk, plus CORRA receivers' FX tags) treat a 156bp overnight policy gap and a 140bp 2Y differential as if USDCAD were still cheap. Spot is only 74th/87th percentile and still negative over 3m. That is not a reversal-grade USD extreme, and it is a noisier, carry-supported expression of US-rate persistence. Rates remain cleaner; the fight is direction of leftover US 2027 hikes, not whether to mix in CAD labor 38 or oil beta.

value-guy and perma-bull attack Canada cheapness from opposite CRA sides. Both miss that CORRA 2.29 versus SOFR 3.85 is the level that makes CA-US 2Y look historically cheap. Fading that spread or paying Mar-27 CORRA is not a cleaner statement of post-FOMC US event-premium decay. Keep the book on SR3H7, not on a CA-US RV and not on paying CRA.
defense: VERIFIED ANCHOR: overnight SOFR 3.85 after a delivered, >90% priced 25bp hike; SR3H7 implied 4.58 still prices ~73bp of extra tightening; Dec-26 already 4.32; US 2Y 4.76 is the 100th percentile 1y after +57bp 1m; Saudi STS reduced the extreme oil-supply tail; US gauges remain 72/75 so this is not a growth-break dove call. INFERENCE: residual Mar-27 premium is the crowded energy-hawk overlay, not the minimum path required by the printed 25bp. Plausible normalization is partial giveback toward packet Dec-26 4.32, not a collapse to 3.85. UNKNOWN: CME SR3/UST positioning and whether the next CPI/labor print re-arms a Dec-26 hike. That unknown is why size stays 40m of 100m, not a reason to pay the squeeze.

Do not fade merely because the 2Y printed a z-score. The reversal condition is the event now sitting in the overnight benchmark plus a reduced oil-supply tail against leftover 1H27 steps. Independent checks remain SOFR/SR3 path, US 2Y, 2s10s front-end flattening, still-hot gauges (which CAP size), and the oil-news split (tail reduced, residual energy risk preserved). Flow cannot be invoked as the squeeze's cause: CME_positioning is missing.

Rates stay selected versus short USDCAD: the discrepancy lives in the US policy path; USDCAD is only modestly rich and is carry-opposed as a fade. Alternative rates RV (pay CORRA vs receive SOFR to fade CA-US 2Y at -140bp) remains inferior because the 156bp overnight gap is the anchor. Sidecar open_positions is still [].

Concession, not withdrawal today: thesis is wrong if the next 25bp is clearly re-armed and delivered into the Dec-26 SR3 window while SR3H7 implied holds at or above the packet Jun-27 mid 4.72, or if US labor/inflation hard inputs re-accelerate from the retained Aug-26/Jul-26 prints and the oil-supply tail re-widens. Chop around 4.58 without a new hike signal is wrong-timing: extend horizon rather than add, rather than flip to trend-follower's pay. Book intent unchanged: OPEN 40m long duration SOFR_2027-03 at packet mid only.

context_build.causal_mechanism: After a fully priced 25bp hike, remaining front-end yield squeeze is the market still converting a known FOMC outcome plus an energy-shock narrative into extra 2027 hikes. Mean reversion requires that additive premium to fade once (i) the overnight benchmark has already jumped with the hike and (ii) the extreme oil-supply tail that justified more tightening is reduced. The trade tests whether Mar-27 SOFR implied (4.58) still needs ~three extra 25bp steps beyond the new 3.85 SOFR fixing, or whether that path was an overshoot around a known event.
context_build.path_to_current_price: Verified path: Reuters recorded >90% probability of a 25bp hike into the Sep-16 FOMC; the Fed delivered 25bp to 3.75–4.00%; NY Fed SOFR was 3.62 on 2026-09-16 and 3.85 on 2026-09-17; US 2Y as of 2026-09-18 is 476bp, 100th percentile of the 1y sample, +9bp 1d (z 1.90) and +57bp 1m (z 3.29); SR3 strip as of the funding/tradable layer is 4.00 (2026-09), 4.32 (2026-12), 4.58 (2027-03), 4.72 (2027-06), peaking at 4.755 (2027-09). US 2s10s as of 2026-09-17 is +56bp, 0.6th percentile 1y, -18bp over 1m—the curve footprint of the same front-end selloff. Desk last-24h thesis: energy shock is keeping term-rate pressure elevated even where domestic growth is softer, reinforced by BoJ +25bp to 1.25% and a 6–3 BoE hold with three hike votes.
context_build.known_vs_new_information: Known before the cutoff: August CPI had already kept a Fed tightening bias; the Sep-16 hike itself was >90% priced. New or newly transmitted: the hike actually printed and SOFR jumped 23bp into 3.85; Saudi ship-to-ship crude via Oman reduced the extreme oil-supply tail; US 2Y continued to 476bp / 100th percentile after the decision rather than giving back the event premium. A known hike cannot explain a new 1m 3.3-sigma 2Y squeeze unless the market is still adding an energy/global-tightening overlay on top of the already-priced 25bp.
context_build.market_implied_assumption: SR3H7 at 4.58 versus SOFR 3.85 prices about 73bp of additional tightening by Mar-27 (roughly three more 25bp steps). SR3M7 at 4.72 and SR3U7 at 4.755 extend that to ~87–90.5bp by mid/late 2027. The sovereign 2Y at 4.76 is consistent with that 12m implied peak. Price therefore requires that US inflation/labor stay hot enough, and the energy shock persist enough, to deliver a multi-hike cycle after Sep-16—not a one-and-done.
context_build.market_assumption_disagreed_with: Disagree that the residual 73bp of Mar-27 hike premium is still required now that the Sep hike is in the overnight fixing and the extreme oil-supply tail has been reduced. The disagreement is not that the Fed has become dovish, nor that US gauges are weak; it is that the post-decision front end overshot a known 25bp by converting a fading oil tail and global hawkish headlines into extra 2027 hikes.
context_build.price_decomposition: Level versus change: overnight SOFR 3.85 is the new policy floor (level); the 1m +57bp in US 2Y and the +73bp SR3H7-over-SOFR spread are the change/premium. Tenor: the mispricing is in 1H27 SOFR (Dec-26 4.32 already contains the next hike; Mar-27 4.58 and Jun-27 4.72 are the additive steps). Curve: 2s10s flattened 18bp over 1m to a 1y extreme, so the marginal driver is the front end, not a parallel long-end term-premium shock. Cross-market: CA 2Y 327bp (98th percentile 1y) fell 8bp on the latest CA observation while US 2Y rose 9bp, so the squeeze is US-led rather than a uniform G10 hike. AU 2Y 499.9bp (99th percentile) is a separate housing/inflation story, not this trade.

historical_reference.distribution: US 2Y 476bp sits at the 100th percentile of the packet 1y (n=252) distribution with z 2.89; the 1m change of +57bp has z 3.29 on that same 1y change distribution. US 2s10s +56bp is the 0.6th percentile 1y (z -2.00) after a -18bp 1m flattening, but only the 65.5th percentile over 5y—so the curve extreme is a 1y-window fact, not a 5y inversion. CA-US 2Y at -140bp is the 3.8th/4.3rd percentile (1y/5y) and is cited as a discovery contrast: Canada is historically cheap versus the US because overnight CORRA 2.29 versus SOFR 3.85 already anchors a ~156bp policy gap, so that spread extreme is not this fade.
analogs: Closest supplied analog set is US 2s10s 1m flattening of -18bp (2026-09-17). 2024-02-26: level -71bp, prior 1m -18, forward 1m +4bp / 3m +7bp (modest subsequent steepening from a deeply inverted starting point). 2022-04-08: level +20bp, prior 1m -18, forward 1m +13bp / 3m -21bp (1m steepening then 3m re-flattening). 2022-12-14: level -91bp, prior 1m -18, forward 1m +20bp / 3m +14bp (steepened). 2023-05-30: level -99bp, prior 1m -18, forward 1m -31bp / 3m -11bp (kept flattening). Two of four same-pace flattenings steepened in the next month; one kept flattening hard. The packet does not attach named historical_move_analogs directly to the US_2Y +57bp 1m level series; that absence is explicit.

Secondary analog on the related CA-US 2Y 1m move of -17bp: 2025-01-30 at almost the same spread level (-145bp) then forward 1m -5bp / 3m +25bp (spread mean-reverted over a quarter). 2024-12-18 at -130bp then 1m -3 / 3m -20 (spread cheapened further). Mixed, so the CA-US screen is not used as the trade.
historical_reference.regime_differences: The 2022–23 2s10s analogs were often already inverted (levels -71 to -99bp) during a still-early hiking cycle with inflation far above target; today's 2s10s is positively sloped at +56bp after a 25bp hike that was >90% priced and with Core PCE described in the retained US inflation gauge as only modestly hotter than policy-neutral (Jul-26 +0.2% m/m). Aug-26 unemployment 4.1% unchanged, AHE +0.3% m/m / +3.1% y/y, payrolls +162k. BoJ has just hiked to a 31-year high 1.25% and BoE split 6–3, a more globally hawkish overlay than several 2024 analog dates. Energy-shock plumbing (pipeline attack then Saudi STS workaround) has no clean one-for-one match in those 2s10s episodes. Therefore analogs support only a partial front-end giveback, not a full unwind to pre-hike SOFR 3.62.

That is the same energy-hawk overlay in Canada, but the overnight gap versus SOFR is an anchor, so Canada is triangulation not the expression.
